_metadata.independence: I read only the brief and x17-rb-input.json; I opened no other file, did not search the repository and did not use the web.

hints.reason: AIR via the Nike Air shoe line and VICTORY via Nike the Greek goddess of victory: a clean brand/myth double meaning with a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; both senses of NIKE are widely known.

hints.reason: ANT via The Ant and the Grasshopper and WORK via the fable's hard-work-versus-play moral; the work side is a step further but the fable is very familiar.

pairs.pair_note: WORK side leans on the fable's moral rather than a direct name; still fair.

hints.reason: CRASH via Crash Bandicoot and AUSTRALIA via bandicoots being Australian marsupials; the game character makes the hint word familiar and the animal fact pays off.

pairs.pair_note: Nice game-plus-nature pairing.

hints.reason: BAG via sack meaning a bag and FOOTBALL via the quarterback sack: a clear, honest double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Clean and easy.

hints.reason: BAT via Ozzy's infamous 1982 bat-biting incident and HEAVY via his heavy metal career with Black Sabbath; both are famous pop-culture facts.

pairs.pair_note: Well-known rock lore; lines are accurate and hedged.

hints.reason: BED via oyster beds and PEARL via pearls forming in oysters; both links are familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Solid, easy clue.

hints.reason: BIRD via The Birds and SHOWER via Psycho's shower scene; two of the most famous Hitchcock images.

pairs.pair_note: Classic film pairing that clicks immediately.

hints.reason: BLOOD via blood plasma and STATE via plasma as a state of matter; a satisfying science double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; STATE is a nicely disguised target.

hints.reason: SHARK via Spielberg's Jaws and BOND via Jaws the steel-toothed henchman (The Spy Who Loved Me, Moonraker); both are well-known references.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent two-film double reference; the Bond side gives a real aha.

hints.reason: CAT and BOX both via Schrodinger's cat sealed in a box; one reference covers both, and it is widely known.

pairs.pair_note: Fair and familiar; spelling without the umlaut is fine.

hints.reason: BUBBLE via boba (bubble) tea and STAR WARS via Boba Fett; two unrelated worlds meeting in one word.

pairs.pair_note: Fun, modern and fair.

hints.reason: CAGE via Nicolas Cage and TREASURE via his signature film National Treasure; the first name points straight at Cage and the film is one of his best known.

pairs.pair_note: Simple actor-plus-film clue; works.

hints.reason: CANDY via candy corn and SCARECROW via scarecrows in cornfields; the autumn/Halloween theme makes the pairing feel cohesive.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join on the candy side but instantly familiar and thematically satisfying.

hints.reason: CAR via the Ford Mustang and WILD via mustangs as the West's free-roaming wild horses; a clean double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: BRONCO would also work but MUSTANG is the stronger, more familiar choice.

hints.reason: CHAMPAGNE via the champagne flute glass and WIND via the flute as a woodwind instrument; a neat double meaning with a disguised target.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: CHINA and SOLDIER via China's Terracotta Army of clay soldiers (with a bonus pottery/china echo); route is sound, but the SOLDIER line overstates that every figure is a soldier.
hints.fix: SOLDIER line: Most terracotta figures are clay soldiers, alongside horses, chariots and officials.

pairs.pair_note: Strong history clue; only the per-word line needs hedging.

hints.reason: CLEAN via groom meaning to clean and tidy and WEDDING via the groom; a classic double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Clean (pun intended) double meaning.

hints.reason: COFFEE because espresso is a kind of coffee and SHOT via the espresso shot; easy but honest on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: Easy; hint is a type of one target, which is fine here since SHOT gives a real second link.

hints.reason: COTTON via cotton spun into thread and SUGAR via spun sugar (cotton candy); a neat shared process that also hints at cotton candy.

pairs.pair_note: CANDY would be more obvious; SPUN is the more elegant clue and both senses hold.

hints.reason: CRICKET via Jiminy Cricket and WISH via his song When You Wish Upon a Star; the second side is a satisfying step beyond the name.

pairs.pair_note: Lovely Disney clue.

hints.reason: DEAD via Coco's Day of the Dead story and MEXICO via its Mexican setting; both central to a hugely popular film.

pairs.pair_note: Fair and familiar.

hints.reason: HARD via the film Die Hard is great, but DICE is reached only because DIE is the singular of DICE, which is the mirror image of the banned plural-of-target rule.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: if the owner treats singular-of-target like plural-of-target this is a FAIL; otherwise the Die Hard side is fun and could pass.

hints.reason: Both DOG and EINSTEIN hang on one Back to the Future detail (Doc Brown's dog is named Einstein and rides the DeLorean first); delightful for fans but many players will not recall the dog's name.

pairs.pair_note: Facts are correct; the worry is familiarity, since both sides route through the same fan-level detail.

hints.reason: DRAGON and MOTHER via Daenerys's famous title Mother of Dragons; widely known pop culture even among non-viewers.

pairs.pair_note: The show is adult-rated, but the character name and title are mainstream and the clue itself is PG.

hints.reason: EASTER via Easter Island and HEAD via the moai's nickname Easter Island heads; anyone who knows the word moai gets both instantly.

pairs.pair_note: The word moai is moderately known (helped by the emoji); the lines are accurate.

hints.reason: FAIRY via sprite as a folklore spirit and LEMON via Sprite lemon-lime soda; a crisp brand double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: OLD and FARM both via the song title Old MacDonald Had a Farm; a phrase-join, but as familiar as phrases get.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, charming phrase-join.

hints.reason: TRACK and FIELD via the decathlon's ten track and field events; easy because the targets form a familiar pair already.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but correct; event examples in the lines are accurate.

hints.reason: FISH via bass the fish and INSTRUMENT via the bass guitar or double bass; a classic double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Classic; category targets make it easy.

hints.reason: FLY and SPIDER via the old lady who swallowed a fly and then a spider, with the swallow bird catching flies as a bonus; a fun song reference.

pairs.pair_note: Nice layered clue.

hints.reason: TORCH via Lady Liberty's torch and FRANCE via the statue being France's gift to the U.S.; both well-known facts.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.

hints.reason: HORSE via the Trojan Horse and GIFT via the Trojans accepting it as a gift (echoing 'gift horse'); familiar and satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Strong myth clue.

hints.reason: GREECE via the ancient Greek poet Homer and PLANT via Homer Simpson's nuclear power plant job; two famous Homers with a fun aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; PLANT is a nicely misdirecting target.

hints.reason: HAT via the Mad Hatter is instant, but MERCURY needs the history of mercury poisoning among felt hatters; a lovely aha once explained, yet MAD is broad and most players will reach MERCURY only with real effort, and the MERCURY line never connects MAD to mercury.
hints.fix: MERCURY line: Mercury used to make felt hats poisoned some hatters, and that is often linked to the phrase "mad as a hatter".

pairs.pair_note: Could reasonably pass under the owner's love of indirect aha links; the mercury-hatter fact is a fairly common fun fact.

hints.reason: HOCKEY and LEAF both via the Toronto Maple Leafs NHL team; a well-known team name.

pairs.pair_note: MAPLE or CANADA would also work; TORONTO is fine.

hints.reason: IRON via the band name Iron Maiden and METAL via their heavy metal genre; an instantly familiar band, though the targets are already closely related.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join that works because the band is iconic; easy.

hints.reason: KING and ROLL via Elvis's title the King of Rock and Roll; very familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair.

hints.reason: LIGHTNING and STRIKE both via the saying 'lightning never strikes twice'; an instantly familiar phrase and the lines correctly present it as a saying.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join, but a satisfying one; TWICE is not an obvious word to link to either target alone.

hints.reason: MARCH via the March Hare and TEA via the mad tea party in Wonderland; the March side is a nice disguise.

pairs.pair_note: Good literary clue.

hints.reason: MINE via the Finding Nemo seagulls' 'Mine! Mine!' and SHARK via Bruce the shark; both are iconic moments.

pairs.pair_note: Fun; MINE is a great disguised target.

hints.reason: OLIVE via the martini's classic olive garnish and SPY via James Bond's shaken-not-stirred martini; text avoids claiming Bond's own martini has an olive.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.

hints.reason: POISON via poison dart frogs and PRINCE via The Frog Prince; both familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: RECORD via records spinning on a turntable and TOP via the spinning top; a clear shared action.

pairs.pair_note: Clean and easy.

hints.reason: ROBOT and TRASH via WALL-E, Pixar's trash-compacting robot; both central to the film.

pairs.pair_note: Route is excellent; check whether the hint can display as WALL-E, since WALLE without the hyphen may read oddly (hyphens are not in the brief's allowed list).

hints.reason: SPORT via sports leagues and SEA via Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea (league as a distance unit); a satisfying double sense.

pairs.pair_note: Good; the SEA side leans on a famous title.

hints.reason: SILVER via silver for second place and TIME via the second as a unit of time; a crisp double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: STONE via the Rolling Stones (and the proverb) and TONGUE via the band's tongue logo plus tongue rolling; a good layered clue, but the STONE line wrongly says the band took its name from the proverb (it came from Muddy Waters' song Rollin' Stone).
hints.fix: STONE line: The Rolling Stones named themselves after a Muddy Waters song, and "a rolling stone gathers no moss" is the old proverb.

pairs.pair_note: Strong route; fix the band-name origin in the STONE line.
